subject: Maths
title: Long division
subtitle: Multiplication and Division (Multi-Digit) · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can divide larger numbers using the long division algorithm (bus stop method).

key_vocab.definition: Long division is a written method for dividing by 2-digit or larger numbers. We work digit-by-digit from left to right.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can divide larger numbers using the long division algorithm (bus stop method).

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Long division -- Long division is a written method for dividing by 2-digit or larger numbers. We work digit-by-digit from left to right.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Repeat the cycle: Divide, Multiply, Subtract, Bring down. Stop when no more digits to bring down.
D → M → S → B
Repeat until done

Key examples:
  ✓ Divide, multiply, subtract, bring down  (DMSB cycle)
  ✓ 672 ÷ 12 = 56  (no remainder)
  ✓ 415 ÷ 13 = 31 r 12  (with remainder)
  ✗ Skip a step in DMSB  (leads to errors)
  ✗ Forget place value alignment  (answer wrong)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – no remainder
  Calculate 672 ÷ 12
  12 into 6? No. 12 into 67? 5 (5×12=60)
  67 − 60 = 7. Bring down 2 → 72
  12 into 72? 6 (6×12=72)
  = 56
  (Answer: 56 (no remainder). Check: 56×12 = 672 ✓)

Example 2 – with remainder
  Calculate 415 ÷ 13
  13 into 41? 3 (3×13=39)
  41 − 39 = 2. Bring down 5 → 25
  13 into 25? 1 (1×13=13). 25−13 = 12
  = 31 r 12
  (31 remainder 12. Check: 31×13 + 12 = 403+12 = 415 ✓)

sections.title: With remainder
sections.content:
Write the answer as ‘quotient r remainder’.

(a) 415 ÷ 13
(b) 500 ÷ 17
(c) 847 ÷ 23
(d) 1234 ÷ 41

sections.title: Decimal answers
sections.content:
Continue past the decimal point until exact.

(a) 35 ÷ 4
(b) 63 ÷ 8
(c) 27 ÷ 5
(d) 100 ÷ 8

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Always divide left to right
✓ DMSB stands for Divide, Multiply, Subtract, Bring down
✗ If divisor doesn't fit, skip the digit
✓ Remainder must be smaller than divisor
✗ 100 ÷ 8 has remainder 4
